_comment: MEASURED SP-1 Track/PLAY resistor-ladder calibration (SAADC AIN0, 12-bit).
Captured on physical hardware with firmware build st16-cal, transport STOPPED,
via cal_service()'s rate-limited CDC capture. This file is the AUTHORITATIVE
provenance for src/st_ladder.c's band table -- the table is generated from
these numbers by the documented rule below and is checked against this file
by tests/test_ladder.c, so a hand-edited band cannot silently diverge.
'centre' is the modal settled value. 'lo'/'hi' are the extreme RAW values
observed while holding that combination. Rows with lo == hi == centre were
held long enough to settle but produced no jitter in the capture window.
IMPORTANT LIMITATION, stated here rather than hidden: these were captured
while the transport was STOPPED. Band CENTRES are resistor ratios and do not
move with playback, but the JITTER figure is a stopped-state figure. The
production decoder is therefore built to fail closed (an out-of-band reading
HOLDS the last mask, it never invents one) and never to latch off.

capture.tempo_line: V11 lib: TEMPO OK bpm_q8=23990 (93.71 BPM) sample_rate=48000 downbeat=16320 frames_per_beat=30733

model_refit._comment: V = F / (1 + 1/sum(1/x_k)); x_k fitted to the four measured singles.

band_rule._comment: half_width = min(25, floor(0.40 * nearest neighbour gap)). Everything outside a band is guard zone and HOLDS.

superseded_claims: st15's st_track_chord.h claimed every chord containing both T3 and T4 was undecodable. MEASUREMENT DISPROVES THIS: T3+T4=1559, T1+T3+T4=1628, T2+T3+T4=1695, all four=1755, PLAY=1813 -- 58 counts of clearance at the tightest point. The claim came from a model anchored on 1335 (the midpoint of the wide 1280..1390 DFU tolerance band) instead of the true T1+T4 centre of 1309.
st15's ST_CHORD_PLAY_FLOOR of 1600 rejected three real, decodable chords.
